title: Rights Written for Every Person
title_ja: すべての人のために書かれた権利

source_links.title: United Nations: Universal Declaration of Human Rights

fact_notes: The United Nations General Assembly proclaimed the Universal Declaration of Human Rights in Paris on 10 December 1948. It contains 30 articles and has inspired subsequent human-rights treaties.

sentences.en: People around the world live under different governments, speak different languages, and follow different cultural traditions in daily life.
sentences.ja: 世界の人々は異なる政府の下で暮らし、異なる言語を話し、日常生活で異なる文化的伝統に従います。

sentences.en: Yet people can still discuss whether there are basic rights that should be respected regardless of a person's country or background.
sentences.ja: それでも国や背景に関係なく尊重されるべき基本的権利があるか、人々は話し合えます。

sentences.en: The idea is that human dignity should not depend entirely on nationality, wealth, social position, or political power.
sentences.ja: 考えの中心は、人間の尊厳が国籍、財産、社会的地位、政治的権力だけに依存すべきではないということです。

sentences.en: This principle became especially important after the terrible experiences of the Second World War, when millions of people suffered.
sentences.ja: この原則は、何百万人もが苦しんだ第二次世界大戦の悲惨な経験の後、特に重要になりました。

sentences.en: Countries faced the difficult task of expressing shared standards without assuming that every society had exactly the same laws.
sentences.ja: 各国は、すべての社会が全く同じ法律を持つと仮定せずに共通の基準を示すという難しい課題に直面しました。

sentences.en: On December 10, 1948, the United Nations General Assembly proclaimed the Universal Declaration of Human Rights in Paris.
sentences.ja: 1948年12月10日、国連総会はパリで世界人権宣言を採択・宣言しました。

sentences.en: The document contains thirty articles describing rights and freedoms intended to apply to all people, not only citizens of particular states.
sentences.ja: この文書には特定の国の市民だけでなく、すべての人に適用される権利と自由を述べた30の条文があります。

sentences.en: These include principles concerning equality, personal freedom, education, work, and protection under the law.
sentences.ja: そこには平等、個人の自由、教育、仕事、法の保護に関する原則が含まれます。

sentences.en: The declaration was designed as a common standard, rather than a single national law that automatically replaced every country's legal system.
sentences.ja: この宣言は、各国の法体系を自動的に置き換える一つの国内法ではなく、共通の基準として構想されました。

sentences.en: Therefore, understanding its historical importance requires distinguishing an influential declaration from a directly enforceable law in a particular court.
sentences.ja: したがってその歴史的重要性を理解するには、影響力のある宣言と特定の裁判所で直接執行できる法律を区別する必要があります。

sentences.en: Although a declaration is not itself the same as a treaty, it can influence future agreements and public discussions.
sentences.ja: 宣言自体は条約と同一ではありませんが、その後の協定や公的な議論に影響を与えることができます。

sentences.en: The United Nations notes that the declaration helped inspire many human-rights treaties adopted over the following decades.
sentences.ja: 国連は、この宣言がその後数十年に採択された多くの人権条約に影響を与えたと述べています。

sentences.en: Its language also gives individuals and organizations a vocabulary for discussing unfair treatment and responsibility.
sentences.ja: その言葉は個人や組織が不公平な扱いや責任を議論するための語彙にもなります。

sentences.en: Nevertheless, the existence of a widely respected text does not prove that every right is fully protected in practice.
sentences.ja: それでも広く尊重される文書が存在することは、すべての権利が実際に十分保護されている証拠ではありません。

sentences.en: People must still examine whether public institutions and daily decisions respect the principles they claim to support.
sentences.ja: 人々は公的機関や日々の判断が、支持すると主張する原則を本当に尊重しているかを調べ続けなければなりません。

sentences.en: For example, a country's laws may promise equal treatment while some individuals still face unnecessary obstacles when using public services.
sentences.ja: たとえば国の法律が平等な扱いを約束していても、公共サービスの利用で不要な障害に直面する人もいるでしょう。

sentences.en: This gap between stated principles and lived experiences is one reason why civic education includes discussion and critical thinking.
sentences.ja: 表明された原則と実際の経験の隔たりは、市民教育に議論と批判的思考が含まれる理由の一つです。

sentences.en: Students can compare ideals with real cases, identify the people affected, and consider which changes could improve fairness.
sentences.ja: 生徒は理想と現実の事例を比べ、影響を受ける人を確認し、公平さを改善する変化を考えられます。

sentences.en: The lasting value of the declaration is not merely that its words were written in 1948, but that they invite continued responsibility.
sentences.ja: 宣言の長く続く価値は、1948年に言葉が書かれたことだけでなく、今も責任を考えるよう促すことです。

questions.prompt: What does the passage mainly explain?
options: Why all countries must have identical laws
The historical purpose and continued influence of the Universal Declaration of Human Rights
How to replace every court
Why human rights were first invented in the 2000s
questions.explanation_ja: 世界人権宣言の成立と、共通基準としての役割・現実との隔たりが主題です。

questions.prompt: Which description of the declaration is correct?
options: It was proclaimed on December 10, 1948, and contains thirty articles.
It was adopted in 2013 and contains five articles.
It is a single country's criminal code.
It requires everyone to speak the same language.
questions.explanation_ja: 採択日と条文数を正しく読み取ります。

questions.prompt: Why is the distinction between a declaration and a law important?
options: A declaration automatically replaces all national legislation.
A declaration can influence policy without being identical to an enforceable domestic law.
A declaration cannot influence any future treaty.
Every court applies the declaration in the same way.
questions.explanation_ja: 宣言の影響力と法的な執行可能性を区別します。

questions.prompt: What does 'a gap between stated principles and lived experiences' mean?
options: A difference between rights promised and what people actually experience
A difference between two languages on one page
The distance between two buildings
A comparison of weather conditions
questions.explanation_ja: 公表された原則と現実の生活経験の差を具体的に言い換えています。

questions.prompt: Why does the writer use 'Nevertheless' in paragraph 3?
options: To claim all rights are perfectly protected
To contrast the influence of the text with incomplete real-world protection
To introduce the date 1948
To explain how courts are built
questions.explanation_ja: 文書の重要性を認めた後、実施の不完全さへ焦点を移します。

vocabulary.definition: rules used to judge what is acceptable
the condition of having equal rights
able to be required by law
connected with citizens and public affairs

grammar.focus: not only citizens of particular states
grammar.explanation_ja: not only は『特定国の市民だけでなく』という対象の範囲の広がりを示します。

grammar.focus: Although a declaration is not itself the same as a treaty
grammar.explanation_ja: Although節が譲歩を表し、宣言と条約の相違を認めながら影響力を述べます。

discourse.role_ja: 帰結：宣言と国内法を区別する必要性
譲歩：文書の価値があっても実施は十分ではない
例示：平等原則と実際の公共サービスの違い

paraphrases.source: This gap between stated principles and lived experiences
paraphrases.rewrite: a mismatch between promised rights and people's actual treatment
paraphrases.explanation_ja: 抽象的な原則と経験の差を、約束された権利と実際の扱いに具体化します。

paraphrases.rewrite: a shared reference point for judging rights and freedoms
paraphrases.explanation_ja: 共通基準を、権利と自由を判断するための共有された参照点と言い換えます。
